note: Replaced on upgrade, never edited in a project. Each row's methods were settled by V31-A11Y stage 1 from the requirements table's proposals; a catalogued row is not a tested pass.

register.title: Accessibility requirements evidence register
register.normative_precedence: The dated normative criterion, definitions and conformance requirements control; concise summaries and informative guidance do not replace them.
register.result_rule: No product has been evaluated by this research report. A catalogued requirement is not a tested pass. Human review, automated evidence and disabled-user participation remain distinct.

axe.title: axe-core
axe.note: Rule tags read as text, never run. A rule is credited to a criterion only when it is tagged to it and is neither experimental nor deprecated; the mapping is regenerated from the version Set 1 pins (stage 3).

features.media: Prerecorded audio or video: audio-only, video-only or synchronized media.
features.moving-content: Content that moves, blinks, scrolls or updates automatically.
features.authentication: An authentication step, such as sign-in or verification.
features.multi-step: A process the user completes in more than one step, on one page or several.
features.timers: Time limits, or sessions that expire.
features.interruptions: Interruptions, such as alerts or pushed updates.
features.pointer-gestures: Multipoint or path-based gestures, or dragging.
features.device-motion: Functions operated by moving the device or by user motion.
features.hover-focus-content: Content that appears on pointer hover or keyboard focus.
features.keyboard-shortcuts: Keyboard shortcuts made of single printable characters.
features.user-input: Forms or other information the user enters or submits.
features.page-set: More than one page or screen, forming a set.
features.languages: Content in more than one human language.
features.exports: Files the product exports for people to use.

axe.tool: axe-core through @axe-core/playwright on each declared UI state, headless Chromium, with the tags for the project's level
axe.evidence: axe results per state, violations and incomplete, with axe's version and the tags run; detects failures of the listed rules only, and an incomplete result files a review row

lint.evidence: lint output with the plugin's version; the rules credited to each criterion are fixed from the pinned plugin at stage 3

snapshot.tool: Playwright ARIA snapshots of each declared UI state against reviewed expectations
snapshot.evidence: snapshot differences per state: roles, names, states, landmarks and headings

contrast.tool: colour pairs measured in rendered states against the adopted digest's numbers
contrast.evidence: each pair's colours, text size and measured ratio, per state

target-size.tool: pointer targets' hit regions measured against the level's size
target-size.evidence: each target's size and spacing, per state

focus.tool: focused-state geometry and pixels at each keyboard step
focus.evidence: per step: whether an indicator is visible, its area and contrast change, and any overlap with author content

text-blocks.tool: blocks of text measured in rendered states
text-blocks.evidence: line length in characters, alignment and spacing, per block

reflow.tool: viewports 320 CSS px wide and 256 CSS px high
reflow.evidence: overflow, clipping and two-dimensional scrolling, per state

text-200.evidence: clipping and overlap per state; indicates text resizing and never proves it

text-spacing.tool: the four text-spacing overrides applied together

reduced-motion.evidence: animations running with and without the preference, per interaction

forced-colours.evidence: content, boundaries and state cues present, per state

orientation.evidence: content shown and operable in both

keyboard.tool: keyboard and dialog journeys with real key events
keyboard.evidence: the journey log: keys pressed, the focus sequence, context changes and outcomes

j-order.tool: reading and focus order journeys against the reviewed sequence
j-order.evidence: the DOM and focus sequence per state against the reviewed one

j-pointer.tool: pointer journeys: cancellation, and single-pointer alternatives to gestures and dragging
j-pointer.evidence: the journey log: pointer events and outcomes

j-hover.evidence: the journey log: content shown, dismissed, hoverable and persistent

j-timing.tool: timing journeys with a controlled clock: time limits, sessions, moving or updating content, interruptions
j-timing.evidence: the journey log: warnings, controls and outcomes against the clock

j-auth.tool: authentication journeys with real paste and autocomplete, never programmatic filling
j-auth.evidence: the journey log: each step, what it asks and how it can be completed

j-multi-step.tool: multi-step journeys that re-enter earlier information
j-multi-step.evidence: the journey log: information asked again, prefilled or selectable

j-forms.tool: form journeys with invalid and valid data: labels, errors identified and suggested, recovery, submission safeguards, status messages
j-forms.evidence: the journey log: messages, their association and announcement roles, retained input, submission outcomes

j-routes.tool: cross-route journeys comparing the set of pages
j-routes.evidence: per route: navigation order, component names, help placement, location cues, ways to reach it

records.tool: the coverage file's validation and the report's checks
records.evidence: the coverage file and the report, validated

vo.tool: Guidepup driving VoiceOver with WebKit and Chromium; headed, serial, attended setup once per machine
vo.evidence: spoken-phrase logs against the expected announcements

engines.tool: Firefox and WebKit re-running the standard specs

touch.tool: touch emulation re-running the pointer journeys and mixing inputs

media.tool: ffprobe stream inventory, caption cue and language parsing, description tracks, player and autoplay journeys
media.evidence: the inventory, cue findings and journey results

pdf.tool: veraPDF with an explicit PDF/UA profile
pdf.evidence: the validation report; PDF/UA alone never establishes WCAG conformance

ios-audit.evidence: audit results; never real VoiceOver use

android-checks.evidence: check results; never real TalkBack use

native-journey.tool: authored XCUITest or Espresso journeys on a simulator or emulator
native-journey.evidence: the journey log per platform and device; never real VoiceOver or TalkBack use

flash-capture.tool: a flash inventory with frame capture for specialist analysis
flash-capture.evidence: frames and the inventory; no validated analyser runs on macOS

ai-review.tool: AI candidate review over screenshots, the DOM and speech logs
ai-review.evidence: the candidates file, labelled heuristic; never a pass

bundle.tool: the dated evidence bundle of each extended run
bundle.evidence: tool, browser, OS and VoiceOver versions, the tree and artefact digests

sheet.tool: the optional review sheet, offered at the keep decision, never required
sheet.evidence: a dated sheet naming who reviewed what

participation.tool: the participation record: recommended, dated, never gated
participation.evidence: a dated record of participant research, or that none was conducted

rows.title: Non-text Content

register.title: Non-text Content
register.applicability_trigger: Non-text content is presented.
register.required_outcome: Provide an alternative serving the equivalent purpose; expose meaningful controls and ignore decoration.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Distinct provisions apply to controls, media, tests, sensory experiences and CAPTCHA; do not give decoration redundant descriptions.

standard.checks: images, image inputs, objects, SVG and meters without a text alternative
images and controls without alternatives in source
non-text content carries the reviewed alternative or is hidden as decoration

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
graphics announce the reviewed alternative
figures in PDFs carry alternative text
alternatives that may not match their context

rows.human: Whether each alternative serves the equivalent purpose; what is decoration; complex images.

rows.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)

register.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
register.applicability_trigger: Prerecorded audio-only or video-only content is provided.
register.required_outcome: Audio-only needs an equivalent media alternative; video-only needs an equivalent media alternative or audio track.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Exception for a clearly labelled media alternative to text.

extended.checks: each audio-only and video-only item has a linked, reachable alternative

rows.human: Whether the alternative is equivalent.

rows.title: Captions (Prerecorded)

register.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
register.applicability_trigger: Prerecorded audio occurs in synchronized media.
register.required_outcome: Provide synchronized captions for the audio content.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Exception for a clearly labelled media alternative to text.

standard.checks: video elements without a captions track

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
caption tracks parsed for timing and language; captions selectable in the player

rows.human: Caption accuracy, synchronisation, speakers and meaningful sounds.

rows.title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)

register.title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
register.applicability_trigger: Prerecorded video occurs in synchronized media.
register.required_outcome: Provide audio description or an equivalent time-based media alternative.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Exception for a clearly labelled media alternative to text; AA also includes 1.2.5.

extended.checks: a description track or media alternative exists and is selectable

rows.human: Whether the description or alternative is equivalent; the text-alternative exception.

rows.title: Captions (Live)

register.title: Captions (Live)
register.applicability_trigger: Live audio occurs in synchronized media.
register.required_outcome: Provide captions for the live audio.
register.exceptions_and_scope: This criterion concerns synchronized media, not a blanket live audio-only transcription rule.

extended.checks: production evidence: who captions live events, and how

rows.human: Live captions produced by people, judged across real events.

rows.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)

register.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
register.applicability_trigger: Prerecorded video occurs in synchronized media.
register.required_outcome: Provide audio description of visual information not already conveyed by the soundtrack.
register.exceptions_and_scope: A transcript alone does not replace this AA requirement; no extra description is needed where the soundtrack already conveys the necessary visuals.

extended.checks: an audio-described track or version exists and plays

rows.human: Whether the description conveys the visuals the soundtrack omits.

rows.title: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: All prerecorded audio in synchronized media has sign-language interpretation.

extended.checks: production evidence: who interprets, and for which items

rows.human: Sign-language interpretation, produced by interpreters and judged by fluent signers.

rows.title: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Where pauses in the foreground audio are too short for audio description to convey the video, extended audio description is provided for all prerecorded video in synchronized media.

extended.checks: production evidence: who scripts and voices extended description

rows.human: Extended description: whether pauses suffice, the script and the voicing.

rows.title: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: An alternative for time-based media is provided for all prerecorded synchronized media and all prerecorded video-only media.

extended.checks: a full text alternative exists and is linked from each item

rows.human: Whether the alternative is equivalent.

rows.title: Audio-only (Live)
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Live audio-only content has an alternative for time-based media that presents equivalent information.

extended.checks: production evidence: who provides the live text alternative

rows.human: A live text alternative produced by people during live audio.

rows.title: Info and Relationships

register.title: Info and Relationships
register.applicability_trigger: Presentation conveys information, structure or relationships.
register.required_outcome: Expose the conveyed information, structure and relationships programmatically or provide them in text.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Covers more than headings: lists, tables, grouping and form relationships can matter.

standard.checks: lists, tables, definition lists and ARIA parent-child structure
labels and structure in source
headings, landmarks, lists, tables and form groups exposed as reviewed

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
structure navigable by headings, landmarks and tables
PDFs are tagged with their structure

rows.human: Whether visual relationships are all exposed.

rows.title: Meaningful Sequence

register.title: Meaningful Sequence
register.applicability_trigger: Presentation sequence affects meaning.
register.required_outcome: Expose a correct meaningful reading sequence programmatically.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Do not demand identical visual and reading order when both preserve meaning.

standard.checks: the reading sequence matches the reviewed meaningful sequence

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
reading order as spoken
PDF tag order is checked by the PDF/UA profile

rows.human: Whether the sequence preserves meaning, responsive variants included.

rows.title: Sensory Characteristics

register.title: Sensory Characteristics
register.applicability_trigger: Instructions explain understanding or operation.
register.required_outcome: Instructions must remain understandable without relying solely on sensory characteristics.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Appearance and location cues may supplement other identification.

extended.checks: instructions that rely on shape, size, position, location or sound
instructions understandable without sensory characteristics

rows.human: Whether instructions are understandable without sensory characteristics.

rows.title: Orientation

register.title: Orientation
register.applicability_trigger: Content has an author-controlled display orientation.
register.required_outcome: Permit viewing and operation in portrait and landscape.
register.exceptions_and_scope: A specific orientation can be essential; preference or convenience does not establish that exception.

standard.checks: content not restricted to one orientation

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
rotation under touch emulation
rotation in the native app; content not locked to one orientation

rows.human: Whether a restriction is essential; real devices.

rows.title: Identify Input Purpose

register.title: Identify Input Purpose
register.applicability_trigger: Fields collect user information from the listed input-purpose taxonomy, using supporting technology.
register.required_outcome: Expose the expected input purpose programmatically.
register.exceptions_and_scope: This is narrower than all form fields; technology support and the specified purposes determine applicability.

standard.checks: invalid autocomplete values
autocomplete attributes in source
fields collecting the user's own data carry the right autocomplete purpose

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Which fields fall in the input-purpose list.

rows.title: Identify Purpose
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: In content implemented in markup, the purpose of user interface components, icons and regions can be programmatically determined.

standard.checks: landmarks, roles and named icons exposed as reviewed

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
icons and regions whose purpose is not exposed

rows.human: Whether the purpose of components, icons and regions is determinable.

rows.title: Use of Color

register.title: Use of Color
register.applicability_trigger: Colour communicates information, actions or distinctions.
register.required_outcome: Provide a visual means besides colour for that meaning.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Programmatic labels alone do not necessarily supply the required visual alternative.

standard.checks: links distinguished only by colour
state and meaning remain with colours forced

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
colour used as the only cue

rows.human: Whether every meaning conveyed by colour has another visual cue.

rows.title: Audio Control

register.title: Audio Control
register.applicability_trigger: Audio starts automatically and continues over three seconds.
register.required_outcome: Offer pause/stop or volume independent of overall system volume.
register.exceptions_and_scope: A whole-page non-interference requirement; turning down the whole device is insufficient.

standard.checks: audio or video that autoplays without control

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
autoplaying audio stops within 3 seconds or has a pause, stop or volume control

rows.human: Every audio source, third-party content included.

rows.title: Contrast (Minimum)

register.title: Contrast (Minimum)
register.applicability_trigger: Visible text or images of text are presented.
register.required_outcome: Meet 4.5:1 contrast, or 3:1 for qualifying large text.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Large means at least 18pt, or 14pt bold, or equivalent CJK size; inactive/incidental/decorative/hidden text and logotypes have specified exceptions.

standard.checks: text below the AA contrast
text pairs at 4.5:1, large text at 3:1

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Text over gradients, images and overlays; the exceptions; axe's incomplete results.

rows.title: Resize Text

register.title: Resize Text
register.applicability_trigger: Text is presented.
register.required_outcome: Allow text enlargement up to 200% without assistive technology and without losing content or functionality.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Captions and images of text are excluded; apply the separate WCAG2ICT interpretation to native software.

standard.checks: viewports that disable zoom
content survives root font at 200 %

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
real browser zoom at 200 % in a headed browser

rows.human: Real browser zoom; whether anything is lost.

rows.title: Images of Text

register.title: Images of Text
register.applicability_trigger: Technology can present the required text appearance.
register.required_outcome: Use text instead of images containing text.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Exceptions for user-customizable images of text and essential presentation, including logotypes.

extended.checks: images that contain text
images of text are customisable or essential

rows.human: Whether each image of text is customisable or essential.

rows.title: Contrast (Enhanced)
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 7:1, or 4.5:1 for large-scale text; incidental text (inactive, decorative, invisible or part of a picture with significant other visual content) and logotypes are exempt.

standard.checks: text below the enhanced contrast
text pairs at 7:1, large text at 4.5:1

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Text over gradients and images; the exceptions.

rows.title: Low or No Background Audio
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Prerecorded audio-only content that is mainly foreground speech, is not an audio CAPTCHA or audio logo and is not mainly musical vocalisation has no background sounds, background sounds that can be turned off, or background sounds at least 20 dB below the speech, apart from occasional sounds of one or two seconds.

extended.checks: background sounds absent, switchable or at least 20 dB below the speech

rows.human: Listening judgement where no stems exist.

rows.title: Visual Presentation
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: For blocks of text a mechanism is available so that: foreground and background colours can be selected by the user; width is no more than 80 characters or glyphs (40 if CJK); text is not justified; line spacing is at least space-and-a-half within paragraphs and paragraph spacing at least 1.5 times the line spacing; and text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without horizontal scrolling to read a line on a full-screen window.

standard.checks: user-selected colours respected
line and paragraph spacing applied without loss
width no more than 80 characters or glyphs (40 CJK), text not justified
text at 200 % without horizontal scrolling

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
real browser zoom and colour selection on blocks of text

rows.human: What counts as a block of text; whether the mechanism serves the user.

rows.title: Images of Text (No Exception)
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Images of text are used only for pure decoration or where that presentation of text is essential to the information; logotypes count as essential.

extended.checks: images that contain text
images of text are decoration or essential

rows.human: Whether each image of text is decoration or essential.

rows.title: Reflow

register.title: Reflow
register.applicability_trigger: Content is presented in a viewport.
register.required_outcome: Preserve information and operation without two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px width for vertical flow, or 256 CSS px height for horizontal flow.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Exception is limited to parts requiring two-dimensional layout; 400% zoom is an equivalent condition only with an appropriate starting viewport.

standard.checks: no loss and no two-dimensional scrolling at 320 px wide and 256 px high

extended.checks: reflow in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Lost content; the two-dimensional layout exception.

rows.title: Non-text Contrast

register.title: Non-text Contrast
register.applicability_trigger: Visual information identifies controls/states or meaningful graphical objects.
register.required_outcome: Meet at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours for the necessary visual information.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Exceptions include inactive controls, unmodified user-agent appearances and essential graphical presentation; not every decorative boundary needs contrast.

standard.checks: component boundaries, states and meaningful graphics at 3:1

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
graphics and states whose contrast may matter

rows.human: Which visual information is required to identify components and states.

rows.title: Text Spacing

register.title: Text Spacing
register.applicability_trigger: Markup-based content supports the relevant text-style properties.
register.required_outcome: Preserve content and operation with at least these font-size multiples applied together: line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2, letter spacing 0.12 and word spacing 0.16.
register.exceptions_and_scope: These are override tolerances, not required default styles; only properties used by the language/script apply. Change no other style property for this condition.

standard.checks: inline spacing that cannot be overridden
no loss of content or function under the four overrides

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Scripts and languages the overrides do not suit.

rows.title: Content on Hover or Focus

register.title: Content on Hover or Focus
register.applicability_trigger: Receiving then removing hover or focus reveals then hides additional content.
register.required_outcome: Keep additional content dismissible, hoverable and persistent as applicable.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Dismissibility has error/non-obscuring exceptions; unmodified user-agent presentation is excepted. Preserve the precise source conditions.

standard.checks: content shown on hover or focus is dismissible, hoverable and persistent

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Finding every disclosure; the exceptions.

rows.title: Keyboard

register.title: Keyboard
register.applicability_trigger: Functionality can be operated by a user.
register.required_outcome: Expose functionality through a keyboard interface without individual keystroke timing requirements.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Exception concerns an inherently path-dependent function, not merely a chosen gesture; native platform services need separate interpretation.

standard.checks: scrollable regions, frames and image maps without keyboard access
every function reachable and operable by real key events

extended.checks: keyboard journeys in Firefox and WebKit
functions operable with VoiceOver

rows.human: Whether every function is represented; path-dependent input.

rows.title: No Keyboard Trap

register.title: No Keyboard Trap
register.applicability_trigger: Keyboard focus can enter a component.
register.required_outcome: Allow keyboard focus to leave; explain any non-standard exit method.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Applies to all page content under non-interference, including content not relied on for other criteria.

standard.checks: focus enters and leaves every component, dialogs included, by standard exit keys or the non-standard method the user is advised of

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
no trap under VoiceOver

rows.human: Unscripted states and embedded content; whether a non-standard exit is advised.

rows.title: Keyboard (No Exception)
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, with no exception.

standard.checks: scrollable regions without keyboard access
every function operable without timed keystrokes, path-dependent ones included

extended.checks: keyboard journeys in Firefox and WebKit
functions operable with VoiceOver

rows.human: Whether all functionality is covered, canvas and drawing included.

rows.title: Character Key Shortcuts

register.title: Character Key Shortcuts
register.applicability_trigger: Content implements shortcuts using only printable characters.
register.required_outcome: Allow the shortcut to be turned off, remapped with a non-printable key, or active only when its component has focus.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Do not treat all keyboard shortcuts as prohibited.

standard.checks: single-character shortcuts can be turned off, remapped or work only on focus

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Finding undisclosed shortcuts.

rows.title: Timing Adjustable

register.title: Timing Adjustable
register.applicability_trigger: Content sets a time limit.
register.required_outcome: Before the limit is encountered, allow disabling or sufficiently broad adjustment; alternatively provide a warning and repeated simple-action extension.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Adjustment spans at least 10 times the default; extension gives at least 20 seconds and at least 10 extensions. Real-time, essential and over-20-hour exceptions apply.

standard.checks: meta refresh with a time limit
each time limit can be turned off, adjusted or extended as the criterion sets

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Server-side limits; the real-time, essential and 20-hour exceptions.

rows.title: Pause, Stop, Hide

register.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
register.applicability_trigger: Content automatically moves/blinks/scrolls or updates alongside other content.
register.required_outcome: Provide the applicable pause, stop, hide or update-frequency control.
register.exceptions_and_scope: The over-five-second condition applies to moving/blinking/scrolling, not the separate auto-update branch. Essential activity exceptions apply.

standard.checks: blink and marquee elements
moving, blinking, scrolling or updating content can be paused, stopped or hidden

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
motion and updates without a control

rows.human: The five-second and update branches; essential motion.

rows.title: No Timing
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Timing is not an essential part of the event or activity, except for non-interactive synchronized media and real-time events.

extended.checks: timing is not essential to the activity

rows.human: Whether timing is essential.

rows.title: Interruptions
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: The user can postpone or suppress interruptions, except interruptions involving an emergency.

standard.checks: meta refresh with any delay
interruptions can be postponed or suppressed

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Finding every interruption; the emergency exception.

rows.title: Re-authenticating
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: When an authenticated session expires, the user can continue the activity without loss of data after re-authenticating.

standard.checks: the session expires mid-task, the user signs in again and the data remains

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: Which data must persist.

rows.title: Timeouts
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Users are warned of the duration of any inactivity that could cause data loss, unless the data is preserved for more than 20 hours when the user takes no action.

standard.checks: the warning states how long inactivity may last before data is lost

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit

rows.human: The real timeout policy.

rows.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold

register.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
register.applicability_trigger: Flashing content is present.
register.required_outcome: Allow at most three flashes in any one-second period, or remain below both the defined general-flash and red-flash thresholds.
register.exceptions_and_scope: Apply defined area/intensity thresholds; all content is subject to non-interference.

extended.checks: frames of each flashing item, for specialist analysis

rows.human: The flash analysis itself.

rows.title: Three Flashes
rows.wording: lab summary of S01; the normative text at the anchor controls
rows.summary: Nothing flashes more than three times in any one-second period, with no threshold exception.

extended.checks: frames of each flashing item, for specialist analysis

standard.checks: autoplaying audio and blinking or scrolling elements anywhere on the page, third-party content included
no keyboard trap anywhere on the page

extended.checks: the standard browser methods re-run in Firefox and WebKit
frames of any flashing content

rows.human: The flash part; regions excluded from the claim.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 2.1.1

register.applicability_trigger: Platform supplies device-independent keyboard services.
register.interpretation: Expose functionality through those services; an on-screen keyboard alone is insufficient.

extended.checks: every function reachable and operable with a hardware keyboard through the platform's focus

rows.human: Every function; an on-screen keyboard alone is insufficient.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 1.4.4

register.applicability_trigger: Native software presents resizable text.
register.interpretation: Support 200%, or the platform resizing capability when it cannot reach 200% for every text type.

extended.checks: Dynamic Type support and clipped text, as Apple's audit reports them
the largest text settings on each platform, no text lost

rows.human: Per-style capability; nonlinear scaling.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 1.4.10

register.applicability_trigger: Native content reflows within available dimensions.
register.interpretation: Use logical equivalent dimensions; a constrained nearest-size benchmark alone does not establish full satisfaction.

extended.checks: layouts at constrained logical sizes, no content lost

rows.human: A nearest-size benchmark alone does not establish reflow.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 1.4.12

register.applicability_trigger: Native technology supports the relevant markup and text-style properties.
register.interpretation: Resolve property support and the criterion conditions; do not assume all native content is exempt.

standard.checks: the text-style properties the platform supports are recorded

rows.human: Which properties apply; no universal injector exists.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 2.4.1, 2.4.5, 3.2.3, 3.2.4, 3.2.6

register.applicability_trigger: A qualifying set of interlinked, separately launchable software programs exists.
register.interpretation: Do not automatically treat screens inside one program as such a set; SUP04 retains useful consistency.

standard.checks: the set-of-programs decision is recorded

rows.human: The set decision.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 1.4.3, 1.4.10, 2.5.8

register.applicability_trigger: Native thresholds use CSS-equivalent logical units.
register.interpretation: Distinguish WCAG typographic points from Apple logical pt: 18pt/14pt bold correspond to 24/~18.67 CSS px.

standard.checks: unit conversions to CSS-equivalent pixels are recorded

extended.checks: contrast and hit regions, as Apple's audit reports them
text contrast and touch target sizes, as the checks report them

rows.human: How the units are interpreted.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 2.4.2

register.applicability_trigger: Software supports screen or window titles through platform services.
register.interpretation: Expose meaningful programmatic titles using the relevant service, rather than prescribing HTML title markup.

extended.checks: each screen exposes a title through the platform's accessibility API

rows.human: Whether each title is meaningful.

rows.title: Native interpretation of 4.1.3

register.applicability_trigger: A non-markup native interface presents status feedback.
register.interpretation: Retain programmatic status feedback as informative native guidance and adopted SUP05; markup-limited applicability must not erase the user need.

rows.human: Whether status feedback is announced and adequate; iOS VoiceOver and TalkBack by hand.
